blockers.quote: Last line inside the image: the next number someone gives you is about the crowd, not about you
blockers.why: Check #12. The planned last spoken line is a lesson, a moral addressed to the viewer, not one real line inside the last image. It also repeats the turn already made at about 78% (line 38), so it reads as a summary. Arthur would deliver it as a teacher's sign-off, which is the sound Riya leaves on.
blockers.fix: End on a line the picture holds. Row three, your pen moving, the bat in the lane. For example: 'Row three. You don't look up. Out in the lane, a bat. Thwack.' Warm, quiet, nearly a whisper. Drop the sentence about the crowd; the turn at 78% already carried it.

suggestions.quote: it didn't lie, it described the crowd and you were never the crowd
suggestions.fix: Say it as short spoken beats with the key word repeated: 'It didn't lie. It told you about the crowd. And you? You were never the crowd.' The landing line stays whole: 'You were never the crowd.' Mark it hushed, then warm.
Add to say.yaml: '0.04%' -> 'nought point nought four per cent'. Repeat the same spoken form every time, since the whole film turns on this number.

Say 'sixty-one per cent', and 'nought point two per cent' for the topper's music chip, so the viewer hears a chance, not a score. Read 'zero' as the word, never 'nil' or 'nought', for the loud boy and the cousin, with 'nought point' only for decimals. Keep one convention.

suggestions.quote: his chip falls to zero the moment he nods
suggestions.fix: Let the picture and the sound carry the fall (a tick, a flap of the counter) and give the narrator only a short beat, such as 'He nods.' Do not add a line that says how it feels; the chip showing zero is already the feeling.

suggestions.quote: seats against applicants for one exam, one number at a time
suggestions.fix: This is the line most likely to read as an essay. Break it into fragments with a question answered at once: 'Seats? Fewer than the people sitting. Applicants? Far more.' Keep it to one number per breath, and give the spoken form of each sourced figure in say.yaml at G2 (for example 'one in two thousand five hundred' for the title).

suggestions.quote: The whole city lit up, almost every chip small
suggestions.fix: Give this beat an emotion tag (hushed, then wry) and a breath-length line, such as 'Every roof. Every window. Every chip, small.' A spoken list of this kind sits well at 1.1x, and the repeated word does the work.

suggestions.quote: Then you see your own: nought point nought four per cent.
suggestions.fix: At 1.1x this is too long for one breath once it sits in the opening. Split it: 'Then you see yours. Nought point nought four. Per cent.' The final word can have its own take, dry and flat.

keep.quote: A number can't lie to you.
it didn't lie, it described the crowd and you were never the crowd
Your cousin's bat thwacks in the lane outside.
